entry.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation
entry.summary:
Video scene graph generation (VidSGG) aims to capture objects and their evolving relationships in videos. This requires accounting for both the persistence of object identities and abrupt changes in relationships. Existing methods aggregate information across frames to exploit temporal context, but an emphasis on consistency can obscure these changes.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics #infosec

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
entry.summary:
For a $Δ$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{Δ/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $Δ\geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In contrast, for $Δ=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #probability-stats

entry.title: Beyond city pairs: Higher-order information in urban growth across borders. We apply higher-order information measures to urban growth across borders and spatial units.
entry.summary:
We apply higher-order information measures to urban growth across borders and spatial units. We analyse 8,808 functional urban areas using gridded GDP estimates allocated from national accounts. Negative estimated O-information occurs in 29.93% of cross-border triplets and 2.00% of domestic triplets.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #complex-systems #combinatorics

entry.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
entry.summary:
When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #combinatorics

entry.title: Vector Commitment Design, Analysis, and Applications: A Survey
entry.summary:
Due to their widespread applications in decentralized and privacy preserving technologies, commitment schemes have become increasingly important cryptographic primitives. With a wide variety of applications, many new constructions have been proposed, each enjoying different features and security guarantees. In this paper, we systematize the designs, features, properties, and applications of vector commitments (VCs).

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics
